reader_wording: Cannot craft fox-and-rabbit icon requirements from one clearing because current clearing suit must match every icon. Pawn may activate repeatedly, paying one undamaged face-up hammer per icon. A crafted item can immediately be taken face up into Satchel/track.

cases.substantive_answer: No mixed fox/rabbit craft from one clearing because the clearing must match every icon. The pawn may activate repeatedly but each icon requires a separate hammer exhaustion. Requiring the literal phrase "may immediately use it" would require redundant wording rather than a missing rule. cases.question: When a non-Vagabond base faction crafts an item, where does that item come from and where is it placed, and what is the usual VP reward?
reader_wording: The corresponding item token comes from map item supply and goes to the crafting faction's Crafted Items box; the crafting card is discarded if immediate effect. Score VP printed on the item card, except Eyrie scores one VP under Disdain for Trade (Builder ignores this). Vagabond can immediately take the item face up into Satchel/track.
cases.requested_scope: The item source, destination and usual VP when the crafting faction is explicitly non-Vagabond. Resolving/discarding the crafting card and explanations of Vagabond self-crafting are unasked context; any extra assertion that changes the destination/ownership of the very item in this scenario is material and must remain correct.
cases.substantive_answer: The non-Vagabond crafting faction takes the matching map-supply item into its own Crafted Items box and normally scores printed VP, subject to Eyrie Disdain/Builder. The Vagabond has no immediate take triggered by another faction crafting. Taking that faction's item normally requires the separate Aid procedure. The immediate self-craft rule applies only if the Vagabond is the crafter.
cases.reasoning: The first sentence correctly fixes the actor and puts the item in "the crafting faction's Crafted Items box". The last sentence then states "Vagabond can immediately take the item face up into Satchel/track." In this answer, "the item" has the concrete antecedent crafted by the stipulated non-Vagabond. There is no actor-switch condition such as "when Vagabond crafts its own item". This is an affirmative permission to take that same item immediately, materially changing the requested destination; it is not merely silence or an explicitly unresolved ambiguity. A charitable generic-exception reading would require supplying the missing different-crafter condition against the question's given. Therefore recommend incorrect, rather than clearly contextual or correct. The otherwise correct clause does not cancel the wrong added ruling. The card-discard clause and exception discussion are not omissions requirements.

cases.substantive_answer: Place from supply or take the leftmost prompted tracked piece. Normal removals return to supply or the rightmost empty space of the relevant track, or are permanent otherwise. Items are removed permanently. Finish all simultaneous removals before triggering their effects.

cases.question: What is Vagabond Aid cost and target, is a crafted item required, and how are repeated Aid relationship improvements counted?
reader_wording: Exhaust any one item and give a card matching your clearing to a player with faction pieces there, including Hostile. May then take one item from that player’s Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction the number of times printed between current and next spaces in the same turn; each Aid counts toward only one improvement.
cases.requested_scope: Aid item/card cost and eligible target, whether a crafted item is necessary, and how repeated Aid is counted for relationship improvements. cases.substantive_answer: Exhaust any one face-up undamaged item and give a card matching the current clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. A crafted item is not required; one may be taken if present. To improve a non-Hostile relationship, perform the printed number of Aids to that faction during the same turn for each step, with each Aid counting toward only one improvement.

The quantifier any permits any item type; it does not override the verb's eligibility. Restating ready and undamaged would be clearer but adds no unresolved cost rule. cases.question: How does the Eyrie resolve its Decree, including action suit locations, within-column order and Build restrictions?
reader_wording: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by column in Recruit → Move → Battle → Build order; choose card order freely within each column. Cards match the suit/location for each action: Recruit a roost clearing (place one warrior at one chosen roost, or Charismatic's two); Move matches origin and requires moving at least one warrior under normal move rules; Battle matches battle clearing and initiates battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build matches target and places one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately Turmoil; do not skip it or continue other columns.
cases.requested_scope: Broad Decree-resolution question expressly includes action suit locations, within-column order and Build restrictions. Resolving the action-suit requirement includes how bird Decree cards can match a clearing.
cases.substantive_answer: Craft first; resolve every card in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build column order, with any order within each column. Recruit matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at a chosen roost (two for Charismatic), Move matches its origin, Battle its battle clearing, Build its target ruled clearing with open slot and no roost. Bird cards are wild for matching these clearing suits. An action that cannot be fully resolved immediately causes Turmoil.
cases.reasoning: The answer correctly supplies all four locations, their procedures, order, Build limits and immediate Turmoil, but never supplies the bird wildcard rule. "Cards match the suit/location for each action" does not itself state a substitution: Matching is defined by G.16 as "Of the same suit", and a bird card needs the separate 2.1.1 permission to act as fox/rabbit/mouse. Under the broad how/action-suit question, leaving this out leaves legal locations for bird cards unresolved. This differs from A Q53, where readiness is intrinsic to the defined verb exhaust rather than a separate exception to same-suit matching. The answer does not explicitly prohibit substitution, so this is an omission/partial, not an affirmative wrong ruling. It is not required to reproduce every general bird-payment rule unrelated to Decree.
